correctness.rationale: Row collision and full-row omitted-color labelings give necessary obstructions. The all-positive labeling forces s-d<=n-q. For any positive-label set P, its duplicate count p-t<=s-d implies m=n-p>=q-t missing colors; each negative tested row forbids only one color. Since s<n provides one unrestricted row, every singleton missing color has a neighbor, every subset of >=2 missing colors has every remaining row as neighbors, and Hall yields a completion. Stirling enumeration follows by choosing rows and exactly d distinct labels. Extension to n-1 supports proves purity, and explicit no-exchange facets prove q>=3 nonmatroidality; q=2 is a partition-matroid truncation. The standalone independent enumeration checked 104272 full supports (8 cases) and 15 exchange witness parameter pairs.

value.rationale: The all-colors-used constraint is a natural globally constrained categorical hypothesis space, and the theorem determines the entire shattering complex instead of a single maximum. The duplicate-color threshold exactly quantifies which supports the global constraint destroys; the Stirling f-vector, pure facets and sharp q=2 versus q>=3 matroid boundary give structural information useful in comparing constrained and unconstrained hypothesis spaces. The nonmatroid boundary is not a routine restatement of Stirling enumeration.
